title: Define discovery-to-serving contract for exploratory community models with telemetry gates
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Clarify the end-to-end contract that takes a newly discovered community (third-party) model from catalog discovery through to serving on Redwood with lightweight telemetry gates and a soft-pinning lifecycle. This ticket defines the required signals, experiment windows, automated actions, and operator-visible checkpoints so engineering can implement a safe incremental rollout path for exploratory models.
background: We routinely ingest community models that are useful to users but may have unknown runtime characteristics (sequence length patterns, attention kernel compatibility, tokenization edge cases). Current intake lists compatibility and pinning as policies but lacks an explicit telemetry contract that drives automated soft-pin or quarantine decisions. This increases manual work for SRE/Runtime teams and delays making useful models available.
requirements: Define a minimal telemetry signal set (latency p50/p95 by seq-len bucket, failure rate, OOM errors, kernel fallback count, kv-cache hit ratio) required before an exploratory model graduates to unpinned serving

Specify instrumentation points in the serving runtime (request metadata, kernel selector tags, quantization path trace) and the data retention window (default: 72 hours for intake ramp) for admission decisions
Define automated soft-pin actions: criteria to apply temporary pin to a specific runtime variant, automatic release conditions, and manual override hooks for SRE/PM
Outline a discovery rollout timeline: discovery -> experimental routing (1% traffic) -> telemetry evaluation window (72h) -> gated unpinned serving or soft-pin/quarantine
Document operator-visible dashboards and alert thresholds used to escalate high-severity issues during intake
Provide clear acceptance criteria and a rollback playbook for runtime regressions discovered post-unpinned rollout
acceptance_criteria: Catalog ingestion flow emits the agreed telemetry signals for 100% of test requests in the experimental routing path
Telemetry dashboard shows latency by sequence-length bucket and kernel-fallback counts within 24 hours of experimental routing starting
Soft-pin automation is implemented as a config rule (matchable by model id and runtime tag) that can be triggered by telemetry thresholds without code deploy
Operator runbook created and linked from model catalog entry; includes immediate rollback steps, required Slack channels, and owners
E2E test (GitHub PR) simulates a model that triggers soft-pin and validates automatic application and subsequent automatic release after stability window
No customer-facing traffic is routed to an unpinned model variant unless telemetry window has passed or a PM sign-off exception is recorded
out_of_scope: Full formal certification of third-party weights (legal/licensing checks) and extended long-term quality monitoring beyond the initial intake window (that will be covered by separate lifecycle work).
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Use a 72-hour telemetry window as a balance between statistical confidence and speed-to-serve; risk: some rare regressions may be missed and handled by rollback
Tradeoff: Prefer lightweight signal set to keep ingestion fast vs. deep instrumentation which slows rollout; we will iterate and add signals once baseline is stable
Decision: Automate soft-pin as an infra config rule rather than code path to reduce deploy friction for emergency responses
implementation_notes: Runtime engineering needs to expose kernel selector tags and OOM/fallback counters via the unified traces API
Catalog ingestion service must annotate model entries with an 'experimental_route_id' so traffic splits are auditable
Console team to add a temporary experimental intake dashboard and a read-only view for the Security team
Ops to own initial alert thresholds; PM + Runtime to define escalation matrix
